newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Economic Times
ITC TO PAY 5 PCT ROYALTY FOR MAKING BAT BRANDS

ITC Ltd will pay a royalty of five percent to the B.A.T. Industries plc (BAT) company to manufacture a few of its international cigarette brands through a licensing arrangement. Under the pact, ITC will make overseas brands like 555 and Benson & Hedges in Bangalore. Although the details of the agreement are under wraps, the indications are that ITC and BAT have embarked on a venture with a long-term perspective. The timetable of the agreement has been set in a manner to benefit ITC shareholders. The agreement says BAT will continue to offer its brands for manufacture in India for at least 30 years.
The Times Of India
LALOO YADAV CHARGESHEETED BUT REFUSES TO QUIT

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday filed a 50-page chargesheet against Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav and other 55 politicians and bureaucrats in the $280-million "fodder" scam. Meanwhile a CBI special judge turned down Yadav's plea for an interim stay on his arrest. The court also reserved its order on an anticipatory bail application filed by Yadav. The order will be passed on Wednesday. Reacting to the chargesheet Yadav said he would not resign unless the accusations were proved in court.
Business Standard
LIQUIDITY SURGE TRIGGERS CRASH IN GILT YIELDS

Increased liquidity in the banking system sent yields on government paper crashing across the board. Securities issued in the current fiscal were quoted at a premium of 1.40 rupees to three rupees. Aggregate bank deposits increased by 105.21 billion rupees during fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). But the corresponding rise in bank credit was lower at 20.11 billion rupees. With no avenue to park their funds banks made a beeline for the secondary market leading to a drop in yield on gilts. In the second fortnight of May alone deposits increased by 40.32 billion rupees.
5-8 PCT PETROL, DIESEL PRICE HIKE LIKELY

Reforms in the oil sector to be announced next week may include an immediate five percent to eight percent increase in the prices of petrol, diesel and kerosene. The administered price mechanism may be abolished by the year 1999 or 2000. Total decanalisation of crude oil and petroleum product imports by 1998/99 and a phased reduction of import duty on crude oil and petroleum products from 1998 onwards are also likely. The new package of measures may rise the price of petrol by two rupees per litre and that of diesel by 1.80 rupees a litre.
Financial Express
IFCI PLANS $150 MLN GDR ISSUE, RESULTS ON THURSDAY

The Industrial Finance Corporation of India Ltd (IFCI) has drawn up plans for a $150 million Global Depository Receipt (GDR) issue. The pricing and the date of launch will be decided on June 26. The IFCI is consulting a number of international investment banks quietly on its GDR issue. It has drawn up a short-list of investment banks likely to be assigned the mandate. The IFCI wants to raise between four and five billion rupees from the international market during fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).
The Economic Times
FINANCE FIRMS CAN PICK UP ERRING TELECOM CIRCLES

Financial institutions will have the first right to pick up a new operator for a telecom circle if the existing basic service licence holder defaults. The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has included this condition in a revised tripartite agreement. DoT will discuss all issues related to the assignability and licence agreement with basic telecom operators on Tuesday.
The Observer
RESERVE BANK DIRECTIVE ON GOLD IMPORT

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday directed scheduled commercial banks to submit their applications if they wanted to import gold, silver or platinum for supply to certain eligible categories. The RBI also asked the banks to send along with their application a note explaining the arrangements planned by them for transacting on these metals. The government earlier announced that banks will be allowed to import gold. But the banks were not very interested.
Financial Express
DIVIDEND WARRANT FACILITIES MAY BE TREATED AS CREDIT

The State Bank of India is planning to treat dividend and interest warrant facilities offered to corporates including a large number of non-bank finance companies as a credit facility. Once this is done the corporates will be required to offer collateral and even a charge on current assets to access the facility. The Bank is likely to treat the interest warrant facility as a contingent liability in its books on the lines of letters of credit and guarantees. The bank is also considering the possibility of pushing up the cash margin requirement for the facility and demanding collateral. Now the cashing of dividend warrants is treated as a pre-funded facility.
Business Standard
FIs SEEK GREATER ROLE IN L&T AFFAIRS
Financial institutions are seeking to play greater role in the affairs of the engineering major, Larsen & Toubro, (L&T), by increasing their representation on the company's board.
The Economic Times
SATELLITE COMMUNICATIONS TO BE OPENED UP

The government has decided to open up the satellite communications sector to the private sector as well as allow the use of Indian satellites by the private sector. A law effecting this will soon be formulated. But foreign investment in the sector will be limited to uplinking facilities. Indian companies will be allowed to set up satellite communications facilities and use them to their benefit. But foreign channels will not be allowed to use earth stations except in special cases. The government also plans to privatise Indian satellites (Insat) and permit Indians to own and operate satellite systems in the country.
The Observer
10 POWER PROJECTS UNLIKELY TO TAKE OFF IN 9TH PLAN

Of the 13 major power projects earmarked by the National Thermal Power Corporation for commissioning during the Ninth Five-year Plan 10 are unlikely to take off, say sources in the power ministry. The Central Electricity Authority has not even conducted the techno-economic feasibility study for these projects. For the Faridabad Gas project, the corporation is yet to finalise the site. The Kawas II and Auralya projects of 650 mw each face problems of fuel linkages. Doubts are being expressed about the feasibility of the Hyderabad Metro 650 mw power project because the city is cyclone-prone.
Business Standard
OFFICIALS TO BE QUESTIONED ON CRB SCAM

The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance will question Finance Ministry officials on Monday to establish the causes of the 12 billion-rupee CRB Capital Markets scandal involving the failed firm that saw a run on its deposits. The committee may also suggest measures to prevent similar scams in future.
Financial Express
THAPAR REMOVED FROM BOARD OF PHOENIX PULP

Ballarpur Industries chairman L.M. Thapar has been removed from the board of directors of the Thailand-based Phoenix Pulp and Paper company. The Company is a joint venture between the European Overseas Development Corporation and Ballarpur Industries with the latter holding around 13 percent. Another shareholder, Kirit Shah of Globex Corporation, who holds a nine percent stake too was dropped from the Thai company's board. The decision to remove Thapar and Shah was taken at a recent annual general meeting of the Thai company held in Bangkok.
